hypotheses.rationale: The default learning rate for Token Factory is 1e-5, but LoRA typically requires around 1e-4 to achieve noticeable adaptation. With such a low LR the model only shifts slightly from the base, consistent with the low 14% accuracy despite decreasing train loss.

A LoRA rank of 16 may be insufficient to capture the variability needed for 77 distinct intent labels. Known work shows that higher ranks (e.g., 256) can match full fine‑tuning performance, while low ranks stall accuracy.

Validation loss fell from epoch 1 to epoch 2 but rose again at epoch 3 (1.082 → 1.1954), a classic sign of over‑fitting when training continues past the optimum. More epochs would likely worsen generalization.
The training set contains only 200 short examples (45‑103 tokens) that may not resemble the varied phrasing of real‑world banking queries, leading to good training loss but poor held‑out performance.
